summary: The battle screen renders its presentation registries instead of reading them for labels: a vfx_factory builds a real particle-and-shader effect per presentation.vfx record, camera beats and hit-stop come from presentation.camera, the band rail eases, damage numbers carry weight, the ward line is a drawn shimmering line, grave watch pulses on hostiles, death dissolves, and the paper rigs get a lighting pass that sits them in the plate.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at f5d26d1. Baseline capture read before any code was written (docs/verification/captures/P6-<sha>-00-before.png): the paper rigs float roughly a hundred pixels above the painted terrace floor with no contact shadow, no rim light and no plate colour on them, so they read as stickers on a photograph; there is no effect of any kind on screen -- the vfx registry is consumed only as tooltip prose; there is no camera, no hit-stop and no shake; no damage numbers; the band rail is a flat corner list whose names clip (MICHAEL CORRIGA) and whose Composure pips run off the card; the skill diamonds sit loose on the stone with unreadable grey-on-grey labels; the enemy intent line is invisible against the bright sky; and the paper stage's teal and red layout guide arcs are drawn in the running game. lane/P5-grammar-and-surface had pushed nothing when this lane finished, so game/themes/bronze_vellum.tres does not exist and the prototype's own DEEP/PANEL/CREAM/TEAL/BRONZE/DANGER constants stay the owner of every colour, gathered into one BattlePalette block with a comment naming the Theme as the owner that replaces them.
